text: Those who solely by good fortune become princes from being private citizens have little trouble in rising, but much in keeping atop; they have not any difficulties on the way up, because they fly, but they have many when they reach the summit.
author: Niccolo Machiavelli
locator: Chapter VII, Concerning new principalities which are acquired either by the arms of others or by good fortune
location: Sant'Andrea in Percussina, near Florence, Italy
